stories.title: SO-Arena benchmarks capability spectrum and reliability of System One models
stories.summary: Researchers introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark measuring the capability spectrum and decision reliability of fast 'System One' models across 11 domains, beyond aggregate scores.
stories.more: System One models aim to make fast, general-purpose decisions without generating long chains of tokens, trading deliberation for speed. The paper argues that current benchmarks mostly report aggregate performance, which gives limited insight into how broad a model's capabilities actually are or how reliable its individual decisions are. To address this, the authors introduce SO-Arena, a benchmark that characterizes both the capability spectrum and decision reliability of System One models across 11 domains. The excerpt is cut off before describing results, so it is not yet clear which models were tested or how they performed.

stories.title: G-STAR scales token groups to compress autoregressive image generation
stories.summary: G-STAR proposes scaling token group size quadratically with spatial compression to address the quality-versus-speed trade-off in discrete autoregressive image generation.
stories.more: Discrete autoregressive models are a scalable approach to image generation, but they face a trade-off: long token sequences preserve quality while slowing generation, and aggressive spatial compression speeds things up at the cost of representation capacity. Using product quantization, the authors show that under a fixed information budget, token group size should scale quadratically with the per-axis spatial compression factor. Building on that finding, they propose G-STAR, a method based on this group-scaling principle. The excerpt is cut off before further detail, so specifics on results or benchmarks are not available.

stories.title: PhysLoop uses LLMs' physics knowledge to improve video generation models
stories.summary: PhysLoop is a training harness that uses large language models' physical knowledge to give fine-grained supervision, aiming to make video generation models more physically consistent.
stories.more: Video generation models can produce visually realistic footage but often get physical dynamics and causal consistency wrong. Fixing this normally requires fine-grained physical supervision, such as quality judgments, correction pairs, and controlled variations, which are hard to obtain at scale. Large language models hold physical knowledge but have struggled to reliably apply it to guide video models during training. PhysLoop is presented as a unified harness meant to close this gap, though the excerpt cuts off before describing exactly how it works or what results it achieves.

stories.title: Study asks whether weak decision models can still teach well via RL
stories.summary: Researchers compare three decision models and three general LLMs as actors, judges, and teachers for long-horizon agents, asking if a model that acts poorly can still teach well.
stories.more: Decision models answer a question with a typed output, such as a probability over a set of options, letting one model choose an agent's actions, judge actions already taken, or score actions to train a policy via reinforcement learning. Prior work has mostly studied these models as actors, judging them by how well they perform the task themselves. This paper instead asks whether a decision model that acts poorly can still teach well as a judge or teacher. The authors compare three decision models against three general-purpose LLMs across these three roles for long-horizon agents. The excerpt ends before stating the paper's findings, so it is not yet clear which role each model type is best suited for.

stories.more: Anthropic's status page listed an incident describing elevated errors across claude.ai, Claude Code, and platform.claude.com. The issue drew significant attention on Hacker News, where a thread titled "Claude Is Down" reached 101 points and 83 comments, while a second thread linking directly to the incident report reached 200 points and 147 comments. stories.title: Jensen Huang resigns after 33 years leading Nvidia
stories.summary: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has resigned after 33 years at the helm, with Colette Kress taking over as interim CEO, raising questions about open-source and American AI leadership.
stories.more: Nvidia announced that Jensen Huang has resigned after 33 years leading the company, with the change reported around November 12, 2026. Colette Kress is taking over as interim CEO. The news raises open questions about what happens next for open-source AI and American AI leadership more broadly, though the source excerpt does not provide further detail.
